SY317
Social Policy Analysis
0.5 Credit
Hours per week:
Lecture/Discussion: 3
Social policy is the arena in which citizens, professionals, non-
governmental organizations, social movements, and
government address social inequalities and underlying lived
realities. The
course
explores intersectional power relations and
diverse impacts on Indigenous peoples, women, racialized
people and other social identities. It examines how sociology
contributes to the development and analysis of social policy
and
programs
.
Additional Course Information
Prerequisites
SY280
or
SY281
Exclusions
SY309h
